official_measurement_examples.name: Current national collection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reports 44,373 ancient woodland records from Natural England, while the national inventory is actively being revised.

official_measurement_examples.name: Revised inventory precedence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states that where a county is present in the revised completed-counties dataset, the revised data takes precedence over the older Ancient Woodland England dataset.

official_measurement_examples.name: Smaller sites added
official_measurement_examples.fact: The revised inventory can include previously omitted small ancient woodlands from 0.25 to 2 hectares and separately represents wood pasture and parkland.

official_measurement_examples.name: Inventory absence limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Standing advice applies to ancient woodland and ancient or veteran trees whether or not they are currently shown on an inventory; new evidence can be added.

official_measurement_examples.name: Irreplaceable habitat test
official_measurement_examples.fact: Ancient woodland and ancient or veteran trees are treated as irreplaceable habitats; loss or deterioration requires the exceptional policy test and suitable compensation strategy.

official_measurement_examples.name: Compensation sequencing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Compensation is a last resort and must not be used to erase the need to assess avoidance, direct effects and indirect effects on the irreplaceable habitat.

official_measurement_examples.name: ASNW and PAWS distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data retains separate ancient woodland status categories including ancient semi-natural woodland and plantations on ancient woodland sites, which must not be collapsed into one condition assumption.

official_measurement_examples.name: Wood pasture provisional limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 wood-pasture and parkland inventory is described as provisional and has confidence/extent limitations, so polygon presence or absence is not parcel development clearance.

core_rules: revised ancient woodland data takes precedence only where revised county coverage exists
old and revised inventories must not be silently merged as equivalent versions
inventory absence is not proof ancient habitat is absent
ancient woodland designation is not land ownership evidence
ancient woodland is an irreplaceable-habitat planning consideration not an automatic parcel score
ancient trees and veteran trees can exist outside mapped ancient woodland
ASNW and PAWS status must remain distinct
wood pasture and parkland provisional polygons require confidence context
planning permission does not replace felling or tree controls
felling permission does not equal planning permission
compensation is last resort and not automatic clearance
direct and indirect effects must both be considered
historic or superseded inventory geometry must retain date/version
poor current condition is not a reason to ignore ancient status
no parcel ancient-woodland clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Natural England, Forestry Commission, GOV.UK, Planning Data and Defra sources checked on 2026-07-26. April-July 2026 inventory revisions and provisional wood-pasture data were preserved with version, status and absence limitations; no parcel clearance was promoted.
